subject: Exception catalog + doc curation for Q1 rollout
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: sara@vertexcloud.com
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Exception catalog + doc curation for Q1 rollout

Team —

We have our Q1 rollout target locked to the week of 2027-01-18. Before we commit the launch date to Sales/CS, I need a consolidated exception catalog and a minimal runbook that covers:

- Exceptions we will accept at GA (feature gaps / telemetry gaps / known data patterns)
- Owner for each exception and the SLA for response/escalation
- Required legal/security artifacts for each exception (e.g., SOC2 evidence, SSO scope)
- Rollback/troubleshooting play for infra and model regressions

Ask: can each of you own one lane and ship a short doc by end of day Monday (2026-11-16)? Marissa — can you take the runbook draft. Kimberly — we need a short checklist of legal/security blockers that must be closed pre-GA. Marcus — can you catalog known infra/model exceptions and who to contact on-call? Tessa — please own the rollout decision criteria (go/no-go checklist + rollback triggers).

I’ve looped Sara from VertexCloud to confirm integrations we promised during procurement — if there are any schedule constraints from their side, flag them now.

I attached a working spreadsheet to capture exceptions; feel free to replace with your own doc. I’ll consolidate and circulate a single catalog by Tuesday.

Attachments: exception_catalog_v1.xlsx

Thanks,
Lukas Meyer
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exception catalog + doc curation for Q1 rollout

Thanks — taking the runbook. Quick note on format: I put a lightweight runbook skeleton in runbook_outline_v2.md (attached) so we can keep it scannable. My plan:

1) Triage steps (when a customer hits an exception) — page 1
2) Short diagnostic checklist (logs + kv-cache hits + kernel fallback) — page 2
3) Communication templates for CS/AE + public incident blurb — page 3

I can finish the first pass by EOD Monday. I also populated two example exceptions in the sheet (slow tail latency for long-context requests; tokenization mismatch for some customers).

On the VertexCloud integration — Sara, if you can confirm whether the bulk-sync will be ready to test by Dec 6 that would help schedule end-to-end runbooks.

Attachments: runbook_outline_v2.md

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Enablement
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-15T14:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exception catalog + doc curation for Q1 rollout

Appreciate the clarity, Lukas. I’ll own the legal/security checklist but two quick flags:

- Any exception that involves PII or long-term logs will require a scoped SOC2 artifact and a data-retention policy sign-off.
- SSO changes for partners (VertexCloud) may require an SP metadata exchange and a short security review — I attached the SSO checklist I usually send to partners.

I can get a minimal blocker list by Monday, but full sign-off items may take longer depending on partner timeline. Marcus — I’ll need the exact list of customers that will be in the GA pilot so I can prioritize which contracts need amendments.

Attachments: sso_requirements.pdf

Kimberly Park
Head of Legal & Trust
Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T08:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exception catalog + doc curation for Q1 rollout

Ack — I’ll draft the go/no-go criteria. Quick Q for the group: do we want the rollback policy to be time-based (e.g., rollback within 30 minutes of threshold breach) or impact-based (e.g., rollback if >5% customers experience regression)? I lean impact-based but want the ops team to weigh in.

Tessa Morgan
Group Product Manager, Launches
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: sara@vertexcloud.com, james.lee@acme.com
Date: 2026-11-16T14:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exception catalog + doc curation for Q1 rollout

Uploading the initial exception catalog and my notes (see attached). High-level items populated:

- Model regressions for tokenization edge-cases — owner: Nikhil (NLP infra) — mitigation: pin tokenizer grid + fallback model variant
- Long-tail latency on 16k+ contexts — owner: Infra on-call (INF-ops) — mitigation: progressive rollout + KV cache prewarm
- Partner sync delays (VertexCloud bulk-sync) — owner: Partner Eng (Sara) — mitigation: delayed sync window + compensating retries

On rollback policy: I agree with Tessa — impact-based threshold tied to a short time window. Proposed trigger: if a regression affects >=5% of active GA customers for >15 minutes, we initiate rollback and an incident. I created JIRA INF-4521 to track rollout automation for rollback triggers.

I’ll consolidate final catalog by Tuesday morning after Kimberly’s list and Marissa’s runbook draft land.

Attachments: exception_catalog_v1.xlsx

Marcus Lin
Staff Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
